text:
**Short answer:** The two-week delay doesn't change when DC-EAST runs out of Lacrivia, because it already has. It does push recovery back by 14 days, from about 26 Nov to about **10 Dec 2026**. Until then, the rules say Tier A health systems get stock first, then Tier B, then everyone else pro rata. There is no approved company substitute.

**1. When DC-EAST runs out**
| Pack | On hand 25 Sep | Safety stock | Average shipped per day (last 28 days) | Days of supply | Projected stock-out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FG-1001 Lacrivia 5 mL | 46 | 471 | 36.7 | 1.3 | **about 26 Sep 2026** |
| FG-1002 Lacrivia 10 mL | 34 | 233 | 15.1 | 2.3 | **about 27 Sep 2026** |

As of the 30 Sep data date, DC-EAST is effectively out of both packs.

**2. When supply recovers**
- The next shipment is PO005791: 4,200 units of RM-221 (polysorbate 80, a raw material). S-104 promised to ship it on 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships **21 Oct**.
- It takes 50 days from shipment until finished Lacrivia reaches the DC (plant standard times):
  - 6 days transit to the S-201 premix site (arrives 27 Oct)
  - 10 days to make the CMP-310 premix (6 Nov)
  - 4 days for SEMI-031 (10 Nov)
  - 8 days for the SEMI-044 bulk emulsion (18 Nov)
  - 3 days to fill (21 Nov)
  - 1 day to pack, 14 days of sterility testing and QC release, and 4 days to the DC (**10 Dec**)
- So DC-EAST goes without Lacrivia for about 75 days, from late September to 10 Dec. At current demand that is a shortfall of about **2,750 units of 5 mL and 1,130 of 10 mL**. The delay alone adds about 510 and 210 units.
- The risk is real. S-104 shipped 11 of its 35 closed RM-221 orders in 2026 late, by up to 20 days. It is the only qualified source for RM-221: the alternate, S-131, is not qualified.

**3. Who gets supply first (rule BR-ALLOC-01)**
These figures are Lacrivia prescriptions over the last 13 weeks from clinics in DC-EAST's states (NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC, OH), rolled up to the health system. Clinics get their health system's contract tier.

| Priority | Customer | Prescriptions, last 13 weeks (5 mL / 10 mL) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 – Tier A | Riverbend Health System | 836 (565 / 271) |
| 1 – Tier A | Oak Hollow Health System | 708 (471 / 237) |
| 1 – Tier A | Northfield Health System | 533 (359 / 174) |
| 2 – Tier B | Clearview Health System | 530 (347 / 183) |
| 2 – Tier B | Sunridge Health System | 428 (283 / 145) |
| 3 – Pro rata | 18 other customers, 2,135 prescriptions | Largest shares: Brightwater HS 19.4%, Stonegate HS 15.0%, Sunridge Vision Associates 20 9.3%, Willow Creek HS 8.8%, Harbor Point VA 2 6.5%, Highland VA 26 6.2%. The rest are 5.2% or less each. |

- Tier A needs about 160 prescriptions a week and Tier B about 74. Together that is about 59% of DC-EAST demand of about 398 a week.
- Riverbend and Clearview are headquartered outside the east, but their clinics in DC-EAST states are served from DC-EAST.
- Independent clinics whose names look like a health system's (for example "Sunridge Vision Associates 20" or "Northfield VA 19") are not part of those systems. They get no contract tier and fall into the pro-rata group.

**4. Options and limits**
- **No approved substitute.** Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003) uses the same RM-221 and CMP-310 chain, so rule BR-SUB-01 means there is no company substitute. Medical Affairs would guide alternative treatments.
- **Moving stock from other DCs** needs Supply Planning approval. Stock above safety stock is about 695 units of 5 mL (DC-CENTRAL 363, DC-WEST 332) and about 390 of 10 mL. That covers only about 2–3 weeks of Tier A and B demand. Both DCs also run out in late October or early November, still before 10 Dec, because they depend on the same supply chain.

**Sources and definitions**

**2. When supply recovers**
- The next shipment is PO005791: 4,200 units of RM-221 (polysorbate 80, a raw material). S-104 promised to ship it on 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships **21 Oct**.
- It takes 50 days from shipment until finished Lacrivia reaches the DC (plant standard times):
  - 6 days transit to the S-201 premix site (arrives 27 Oct)
  - 10 days to make the CMP-310 premix (6 Nov)
  - 4 days for SEMI-031 (10 Nov)
  - 8 days for the SEMI-044 bulk emulsion (18 Nov)
  - 3 days to fill (21 Nov)
  - 1 day to pack, 14 days of sterility testing and QC release, and 4 days to the DC (**10 Dec**)
- So DC-EAST goes without Lacrivia for about 75 days, from late September to 10 Dec. At current demand that is a shortfall of about **2,750 units of 5 mL and 1,130 of 10 mL**. The delay alone adds about 510 and 210 units.
- The risk is real. S-104 shipped 11 of its 35 closed RM-221 orders in 2026 late, by up to 20 days. It is the only qualified source for RM-221: the alternate, S-131, is not qualified.
